approved_status: Not an approved drug; US FDA treats it as a dietary supplement (Sept 2025)
reason: Raised BubR1 protein in mouse testes and in SIRT2-dependent mouse cells. Not an approved medicine, so it is the lead to test, not a drug to give.

A SIRT2 inhibitor and the most commonly taken B3 form. In the same paper it lowered BubR1 protein in cells and blocked SIRT2 in vitro (Figure 1). NMN is the testable path; nicotinamide is the one to avoid.
No opened paper shows it raises BubR1.
A different B3 molecule with no BubR1 result in anything I opened. UNVERIFIED as a BubR1 therapy.

At lab concentrations (1 to 16 mM), metformin deregulated BUBR1 and MAD2, caused checkpoint dysfunction and raised genotoxic stress in cancer and non-cancer cells. The mechanism points the wrong way; the paper did not test clinical blood levels.

The mTORC1 signal was allele-specific in mice, present with one truncating allele and nearly absent with a missense allele; the only rapamycin diet note in these mice was preliminary, unpublished and showed no benefit; immunosuppression in a cancer-prone child is a hard objection.
Same class, same allele-specificity problem, same immunosuppression objection.

candidate: Dasatinib plus quercetin and other senolytics
approved_status: Mixed; the pair is not approved for this use
reason: The mouse experiment used a genetic switch (INK-ATTAC plus a lab chemical), not a human medicine, and overall survival was not substantially longer. Removing senescent cells may also remove a tumor-suppressive brake. UNVERIFIED for any human senolytic product.

candidate: SAC, MPS1, ATR and PARP inhibitors
class: Checkpoint and DNA damage response inhibitors
reason: Their purpose is to exploit or deepen checkpoint weakness. In biallelic BUB1B the checkpoint is already badly impaired. The refusal is the direction of effect, not a drug-label quote.
'Binds BUB1B' in a cancer pitch means less checkpoint, not more.
Not approved, and designed to worsen mis-segregation.

direction_vs_BubR1: Context-dependent, in a cytotoxic mitotic-arrest combination
reason: The BubR1 stabilization report sits in a cytotoxic mitotic-arrest context with a mitotic poison. Wrong setting and not approved.
